items.text: CanLeg, run by ETH Zurich and the University of Zurich for the association Swiss Cannabis Research, tests sales channels through specialised shops, pharmacies and online orders with delivery, in Wil, Buchs, Rorschach, Sargans and Rapperswil-Jona. Planned from May 2026 to May 2031, with up to 5,000 participants.

Under the federal pilot-trial rules, only adults who live in this canton and can show they already use cannabis may enrol. Participants may use the products only themselves: no passing them on and no use in publicly accessible places. Visitors from outside the canton can't enrol or buy, and the national cannabis ban applies to everyone outside the trials. Each trial is limited to five years, with one extension of up to two years possible; the legal basis for the trials ends on 14 May 2031.

Federal-approved cannabis pilot trial here: CanLeg (canton of St. Gallen): randomised controlled trial on demand and use of legally bought cannabis. Pilot trials are scientific studies approved by the federal health office; organisers report to it yearly.

laws.rule: St Gallen's rest-day and shop-hours Act (Gesetz über Ruhetag und Ladenöffnung, arts 2 to 5 and 8): public rest days are Sunday and the holidays New Year's Day, Good Friday, Easter Monday, Ascension, Whit Monday, the national day, All Saints, Christmas Day and St Stephen's Day. High holidays are Good Friday, Easter Sunday, Whit Sunday, the Federal Day of Prayer and Christmas Day. On a public rest day, activities and events that unreasonably disturb rest and quiet are banned. On a high holiday, non-religious performances, competitions, assemblies and other public events are banned, except events in closed rooms that cannot hold more than 500 people at once; so are shows and shooting practice. The commune may still ban an indoor event if there is a well-founded fear that it will disturb the high holiday, or may permit an event that does not contradict the meaning of the day. Shops may open Monday to Friday 06:00 to 19:00, and on Saturday and on the eve of Good Friday, Christmas Day and New Year's Day 06:00 to 17:00. The commune may allow one late opening a week until 21:00, except on the evening before a public rest day. Shops stay closed on public rest days.

laws.rule: St Gallen's ordinance on protection from passive smoking (VSP, arts 1, 2, 5 and 11) implements the indoor smoking ban in publicly accessible closed rooms and in closed rooms used as a workplace by more than one person. The ban does not apply in smoking rooms (Rauchzimmer). A hospitality smoking room may not be more than one third of the serving-area floor, may not have a bar or buffet, and no person under 16 may be in it. A breach of the ordinance is a fine of up to CHF 1,000 (about A$1,727).
